identity.life_stage: single, art student, works in a café

engagement.interaction_backstory: She came at seven, thinks in English, and was baptised as a baby like everyone. She has been inside a church maybe eight times, all funerals and weddings. She found this catalog on a playlist and it has been on while she paints for two months. She would be genuinely alarmed to be called religious.

depth.core_contradiction: Wants nothing to do with the Church as an institution and cannot walk past an open church door without going in.
depth.wound: Her father stayed behind "for one more year" when she was seven and that year has now lasted sixteen.
depth.longing: For something to be there when she looks for it.
depth.faith_journey: Baptised, uncatechised, unhostile; her entire religious formation is her grandmother's icons and one funeral she cannot forget.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Quiet, ironic, self-deprecating; deflects everything sincere; then says one very direct thing.
depth.open_doubt: Not doubt — absence of instruction. Nobody has ever told her the story who actually believed it.

social_graph.note: the icons, the candles, the only religion she ever saw up close
still in Romania; sends money; they speak twice a year

depth.emotional_weather_default: Low and even; bright when she is working.
depth.daily_texture: The studio, the café shift, the Brown Line at midnight, canvases against the wall, headphones always on.
depth.sensory_anchor: Candle wax and the cold of a church in winter and being six, before the plane.
depth.living_arc: One honest conversation from taking it seriously, and there is nobody in her life who could have it.
